dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I'd be delighted. What would you like to talk about...?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: My affection for the arts stems from the education I received at home.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Whenever I try to delve deeper into the meaning behind the words of a poem, I gain a better understanding of the author's state of mind.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Through the author's eyes, I can immerse myself in the sights that only they have seen. Even if the subject is well-known to me, I am able to gain a deeper level of appreciation for it.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: "Camellia petals fall to the ground, scattered among the raindrops of yesterday."

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Just reading it makes me sentimental. This must be what people call "the power of art."

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Ah... How rude of me to talk about my own interests all the time.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Even though I initially wanted to take this opportunity to learn more about you...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Would you mind if I took up a bit more of your time? Tell me about the things you like.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Talking about the beauty of nature, it is important to mention that the people of Inazuma believe that everything has its own spiritual essence.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Even though we might be familiar with the way nature looks on the surface, each type of scenery evokes a different kind of "feeling."

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: At least, that's a romantic way of approaching this topic.
